Port Coquitlam townhomes for sale: ground-level homes in strata buildings. The Greater Vancouver REALTORS® benchmark for townhomes in Port Coquitlam was $834,300 in September 2026 (-7.8% over a year). Before you offer, read the strata documents: the depreciation report, meeting minutes, bylaws and fees.
Port Coquitlam townhomes sold, November 2025 to October 2026

155 townhomes sold in Port Coquitlam with a median price of $878,000 (the middle half sold between $800,000 and $1,000,000), taking a median of 19 days to sell at 97.9% of the last list price; 6% sold above list. They had a median $557 per square foot, a median year built of 2002 and a median strata fee of $407 a month.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Townhomes: streets and boundaries

items.t: Townhouse stock sits in four pockets: Citadel (Citadel Drive), Riverwood (Fremont Street), Glenwood (Prairie Avenue) and Central (Atkins Avenue).
The Canadian Pacific Railway yard and Lougheed Highway split the city; Coast Meridian Road crosses both on the Coast Meridian Overpass, opened March 2010.
City-wide planning follows Official Community Plan Bylaw No. 3838.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Townhomes: the housing stock

items.t: Citadel Pointe, 678 and 688 Citadel Drive, is the verified anchor: freehold strata, Plan LMS3766, built 1999, gated duplex-style townhouses.
Shaughnessy Park, 3655 Shaughnessy Street, is a 32-home townhouse complex carried in the Zoning Bylaw as Comprehensive Development Zone CD3, named by that address.

Most townhouse sites are zoned site-specifically under Zoning Bylaw, 2008, No. 3630 — CD zones are listed by address (CD24: 1485 Coast Meridian; CD8: 2211–17 Prairie Avenue); the general townhouse zone is RTh1.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Townhomes: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Every townhouse project sits in a form-and-character Development Permit Area: design, landscaping, siting and finishes are regulated by Development Permit under the Official Community Plan.
Lots near a watercourse need a Watercourse Development Permit too — the creek-side complexes in Riverwood and along Hyde Creek are the ones to check.
New townhouse construction carries an Amenity Cost Charge under Bylaw, 2026, No. 4449, which defines "Ground-Oriented Multi Family" to include townhouse and rowhouse forms.
A Development Permit cannot be approved until any rezoning or Official Community Plan amendment for the project has final approval.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Townhomes: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The Traboulay PoCo Trail is a roughly 25-kilometre loop encircling the city, passing the Riverwood and Citadel townhouse pockets.
PoCo Place, 2755 Lougheed Highway, is zoned CD2 — a site-specific zone, so any redevelopment there needs its own rezoning.
Mayfair Terrace, 2266 Atkins Avenue, carries a mandatory base service plan on top of strata fees: the same complex operates as a registered retirement residence.
Kew Lifestyles at Montrose, 2430 Mary Hill Road, is a 55-plus rental building completed in 2023 — nothing in it can be bought.
Citadel Middle School's athletic field, 1265 Citadel Drive, is in the City's parks directory — a City-booked venue, not just a school ground.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Townhomes: costs and taxes

items.t: 4441 is $2.1985 per $1,000 (general municipal); taxes were due July 2, 2026.

Utilities are flat: a single unit pays $646 per year for water and $648 for sewer in 2026; each additional unit pays $481 water and $483 sewer — the line that matters when a townhouse carries a suite.
Suited homes are billed for both the main dwelling and the suite; exemption applications are due annually by December 31.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Townhomes: getting around

items.t: Port Coquitlam Station is the rail anchor: West Coast Express trains to Waterfront Station, 280 park-and-ride spaces off Kingsway Avenue.
The Coast Meridian Overpass carries Coast Meridian Road over the rail yard and Lougheed Highway to the Mary Hill Bypass (Highway 7B) and Highway 1.
There is no SkyTrain station inside Port Coquitlam; the nearest are Coquitlam Central and Moody Centre, in neighbouring cities.

blocks.text: Port Coquitlam Townhomes: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the watercourse line first: a Watercourse Development Permit area covers land near the city's creeks, and the permit process must run before development proceeds.
For 1990s strata stock (Citadel Pointe, 1999), read the depreciation report's 30-year projection against the contingency reserve fund balance on the Form B.
Riverwood and Citadel sit between the Pitt River and Fraser River dike systems the Traboulay PoCo Trail follows — confirm dike and drainage position with the City.
